text:
maria: Quick question — thinking about a fallback path for gzipped safetensors shards (zipstream) for clients on slow networks. Idea: primary path = index-first range requests + safetensors chunks; fallback = single compressed shard served as a streaming response that we hotfill. Thoughts?

aj: curious, do we mean compressing whole shard files on origin and streaming with content-encoding, or bundling many small chunks into a tar/gzip on-the-fly?

maria: compress whole shard on origin. We already have large shards that are mostly zeros in quantized layouts, gzip helps. Client would detect missing index or range support and use streaming fallback.

nina: main risk I see is atomicity during swaps. If we serve a gzipped blob while a hot-swap/rollout happens, clients could get inconsistent bytes vs index. How do we ensure compatibility?

sam: Can we require a small sidecar manifest header (fixed-length JSON prefix) that lists checksums + byte ranges for the uncompressed view? That would let streaming clients validate as they decompress.

maria: yeah sketch: each gz shard starts with 1KB JSON header like: {"format":"zipstream-v1","uncompressed_size":...,"sha256":...,"shard_id":...} then gzip bytes. Clients reading EOF-less streams can parse header and then decompress/check.

kevin: question — how does this interact with our index-first warmup? We rely on being able to range-request KV pages to populate GPU memory before generation. Streaming a whole blob means you lose ability to fetch individual tensors early.

aj: right. So fallback should be only for cold-start scenarios where range requests fail or are too slow. For steady-state, keep index-first. But we need a graceful degrader that can start streaming into an ephemeral cold cache and still allow incremental activation of tensors.

nina: operationally, streaming fallback should write into our shard cache as an opaque blob then run a background extractor that populates tensor pages from the uncompressed stream into the same page layout. That preserves invariants for later range-based fetches.

sam: we need to ensure that extraction is resumable and idempotent. If extraction fails mid-way (OOM, eviction), clients mid-gen should be able to continue from already-populated pages. So extraction job must mark per-page success with an atomic bitflip (small metadata).

maria: ROI tradeoff: more complexity vs latency wins on edge. We should quantify: simulated warmup latency on 3G -> gz stream reduces time-to-first-token by ~2x for large shards according to the POC. But extract cost is extra CPU and double network egress.

kevin: also think about rollout safety. If we change shard layout between versions, blob header must include a manifest_version and per-tensor layout map. Otherwise extractor will misplace pages.

aj: suggestion: require a stable on-disk canonical layout version (layout_v1) for zipstream fallback. If model changes require layout change, fallback must be disabled for that model version unless we provide a converter.

maria: small config sketch for server side (for ops team):

```
# nginx origin snippet
location /shards/{shard}.gzstream {
  add_header X-Blob-Manifest $manifest_header;
  root /storage/shards/;
  gzip off; # precompressed on disk
}
```

nina: and client detection logic: try range request for index -> if 200+range then use index-first; if 405/416 or range timeout -> fallback to /shards/{shard}.gzstream and trigger extractor.

sam: what about verifying on-disk provenance? We need signed manifests so clients can refuse streaming blobs that aren't signed with model's key. Otherwise MITM or cache poisoning risk.

maria: agreed, header must have signature (ed25519) over the manifest JSON. Clients validate before extracting. That also lets us revoke/blacklist bad blobs by refusing signatures.

kevin: eviction interplay — if extractor is populating pages slowly and eviction policy removes partial pages, we might cause thrashing. Extractor should pin newly-written pages for a grace period and mark them as hot. Maybe use a per-shard extract token that raises priority in eviction queue.

aj: operational knobs: extract-parallelism, extract-priority, extract-pin-ttl. Defaults: parallelism=2, priority=high, ttl=30s. Tune per workload.

nina: implementation note — avoid blocking GPU worker threads. Extraction must be done on separate io/cpu pool and then post memcpy to GPU memory via our existing page ingestion API, which is already atomic and reference-counted.

maria: anything else? Potential negative: storage bloat if we keep both gz blobs and index-first files. Ops will need a lifecycle policy: enable zipstream only for regions with bad latency and evict gz copies after N days.

sam: last thought: metrics. We should emit metrics: fallback_attempts, fallback_success, extract_bytes, extract_time_p50/p95, signature_failures. That will let us decide if feature worth supporting.

maria: ok I'll draft a short RFC with these constraints: header+sig, extractor idempotency, pin-on-extract, layout versioning, config knobs, metrics. Ping @aj and @nina for review. Thanks all. :rocket:

infra-bot: Deployed 2 feature flags: zipstream-fallback (off), zipstream-extract-worker (off). Use /ops/flags to toggle.
